alerts.title: Train derailment at Thurmond
alerts.description: Due to a recent train derailment in the Thurmond area, visitors are encouraged to visit other areas of the park during cleanup activities, which is expected to last through Friday (Oct. 10). Check back here for updates.

alerts.title: Single Lane Closures on South Parkway Near River Farm Drive
alerts.description: Beginning October 8, one lane both northbound and southbound will be closed 24 hours a day and 7 days a week for 4 weeks to repair an upheaval in the road. Please expect slight traffic delays in the area.

alerts.title: Park Central Road East - Side Closed - October 7, 2026
alerts.description: Due to road shoulder debris clean-up after recent storms Park Central Road, from the Visitor Center to Hog Rock Parking Lot will be closed today.

alerts.title: Northbound GWMP Lane Closures Between Spout Run and Route 123 Resumes
alerts.description: Northbound lanes between Spout Run Parkway and Route 123 will close Mondays through Thursdays from 9:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.  from Oct. 5 - 15 for tree maintenance. Southbound lane closures will begin on Oct. 19 and last until Nov. 26.

alerts.title: Bridge to Maryland Heights & C&O Canal CLOSED
alerts.description: Due to safety concerns, the Goodloe Byron Memorial Footbridge to the C&O Canal NHP towpath is expected to remain closed this fall for safety repairs on the pedestrian bridge. This work is in addition to the staircase replacement. A shuttle with very limited space currently runs between Harpers Ferry NHP Visitor Center and C&O Canal Lock 34. This will impact access to Maryland Heights, the Appalachian NST, and the Potomac Heritage NST. We strongly advise considering other trails when possible.

alerts.title: Southbound GWMP Lane Closures Oct. 5-8 Between Tulane Dr and Alexandria Ave
alerts.description: Closures of southbound lanes between Tulane Drive and Alexandria Avenue will detour traffic onto Fort Hunt Road from 9:30 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Mondays through Thursdays from October 5 to 8 for maintenance activities.

alerts.title: Active Closures
alerts.description: Due to recent wildlife interactions and out of an abundance of caution, the Appalachian Trail from Lewis Mountain to Big Meadows is closed to backcountry camping until further notice. The trail is still accessible to hikers. The Naked Creek backcountry zone remains closed for an ongoing investigation.

alerts.title: Temporary Closure of the Clara Barton Parkway 3500 ft of right travel lane
alerts.description: Temporary Closure of the Clara Barton Parkway 3500 feet of right travel lane at Site 17, managed land areas between Clara Barton Parkway and C&O Canal, and between Lock 10 parking lot north to Lock 14 required to address the ongoing safety concerns from DC Water emergency sanitary sewer bypass and pipe repair. Click on "More" below for specific details on the closure.

alerts.title: Burnwood Campground and Restroom Closure
alerts.description: The Burnwood group campground will be closed from October 5 through mid November due to a construction project to replace water lines. During that time restroom facilities will be closed at the Burnwood Trailhead.

alerts.title: Parking Lot E Closed for Construction
alerts.description: Parking Lot E is closed for construction. The park is currently working to expand this parking area, and the lot will be closed while the expansion is being built. Visitors can still access the Mary Byrd Branch Trail and Quantico Cascades Trail by following trail reroute signs and parking vehicles in Turkey Run parking area. For your safety, please follow all closures and only park in designated parking spots.

alerts.title: Rend Trail Closed through December 2027
alerts.description: The Rend Trail is closed for trail Improvements that will include a new parking area, restroom, and a small picnic area overlooking Arbuckle Creek at the Minden trailhead, structural improvements to five historic railroad trestles along the trail, and full trail surface rehabilitation. Additionally, construction of a large accessible ramp over the ‘big rock’ will replace a stairway, resulting in the only fully accessible earthen surface trail located within the park.

alerts.title: Detour along Mount Vernon Trail at Gravelly Point
alerts.description: Due to constriction for the Long Bridge Project, the Mount Vernon Trail will be temporarily detoured around the construction zone beginning on July 15, 2026. Trail users should expect periodic crossings of equipment and materials where the trail meets the construction access road. Detour will be in place through 2030.

alerts.title: Park Headquarters Road is closed
alerts.description: Park Headquarters Road is closed due to rehabilitation work on the Sugarlands water and wastewater systems.

alerts.title: Kaymoor Miners Trail Closure
alerts.description: From June 15 through November 19 the upper part of the Kaymoor Miners Trail (from Kaymoor Top down to the mine site at the junction with the Kaymoor Trail) will be closed Monday through Thursday due to a trail rehab project. The trail is expected to be fully open Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.

alerts.title: Closures: Detours; Towpath; Points of Interest
alerts.description: Multiple items are closed due to hazardous conditions or maintenance. See below for more details.

alerts.title: Infrastructure Improvements to Old Rag Trailhead
alerts.description: Effective May 4, Shenandoah National Park will begin infrastructure enhancements at the Old Rag Trailhead main parking lot. We expect to complete work by November 2026. Until then, the main parking lot is closed to all vehicle and pedestrian traffic. Visitors can access Old Rag Trailhead via existing overflow parking lots. Day-use tickets are still required from March 1 through November 30 in addition to a park entrance fee.

alerts.title: Shenandoah National Park Moved to Fully Cashless Fee Collection
alerts.description: On July 1, 2025, the park transitioned to a fully cashless system at our fee entrance stations. Only credit cards, debit cards, or mobile payments will be accepted.

alerts.title: DC Water Sewer Overflow
alerts.description: DC Water is managing a sanitary sewer overflow from the Potomac Interceptor near Lock 10. Anyone with questions or in need of support can reach out to DC Water’s 24-Hour Command Center at (202) 612-3400 or visit https://www.dcwater.com/about-dc-water/media/potomac-interceptor-collapse.

alerts.title: Equestrian Traffic Temporarily Prohibited - Mile 124.5 to 155
alerts.description: Horses are prohibited between Little Tonoloway (mile 124.5) and Paw Paw (mile 155) due to recent and ongoing towpath resurfacing. See more for details.

alerts.title: Parking at Boundary Access Areas
alerts.description: Visitors are reminded to park in designated parking areas when accessing the park via boundary trailheads. Parking in unauthorized locations may result in your vehicle being towed at the owner's expense. Park on the right side of the road approaching Thompson Hollow. Parking is authorized up to the "No Parking" sign before a private driveway.

alerts.title: Intermittent Lane Closures at GW Parkway for Bridge/Pavement Preservation
alerts.description: Beginning on Monday, November 17, 2025, expect intermittent traffic impacts at GWMP. This Bridge and pavement preservation work is expected to extend into the Fall of 2026 and will make repairs to 24 GWMP bridges and over 30 paved roads and parking assets. To minimize traffic impacts, weekday lane closures on George Washington Memorial Parkway, Clara Barton Parkway, and Spout Run Parkway will NOT be allowed inbound to DC from 5:30am to 9:30am and outbound from DC from 2:30pm to 7:30pm Monday through Friday.

alerts.title: Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road closed.
alerts.description: Straight Fork and the one-way section of Balsam Mountain Road (Heintooga Round-Bottom Road) are closed.

alerts.title: Get Skyline Drive Status Updates
alerts.description: Sign up for Shenandoah Alerts by texting SHENALERTS to 888777. Any time there are closures, re-openings, or other important safety-related alerts, subscribers will receive a notification via text. You may unsubscribe at any time.

alerts.title: Ongoing work on Lower Town buildings
alerts.description: Facilities staff are doing repair work on several buildings in Lower Town. Please follow signs for alternate entrances and heed temporary closures.

alerts.title: Hiking in Gold Mine Tract
alerts.description: Visitors are restricted to the designated trails within the Gold Mine Tract in the Great Falls area. This location is generally defined as that area bordered by MacArthur Boulevard and Berma Road and depicted on the Great Falls Maryland Hiking Map.

alerts.title: Most visitors need a parking tag
alerts.description: All vehicles parking for longer than 15 minutes require a parking tag. Three tag durations are available for purchase for all vehicle sizes and types: Daily ($5), Weekly ($15), or Annual ($40).

alerts.title: Ticket Required to Hike Old Rag
alerts.description: March 1 - November 30 those wishing to hike Old Rag are required to obtain a day-use ticket before arriving.

alerts.title: Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway closed from Canyon Junction to Great Arch Pullout
alerts.description: The Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway is currently closed from Canyon Junction to Great Arch Pullout to all pedestrian, bicycle, and vehicle traffic. Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway is open from East Entrance to Great Arch Pullout. There will be no through traffic until further notice.

alerts.title: Parking lot repairs, October 5-16
alerts.description: The following parking lots will be closed for short periods for maintenance work: Frazee House & Jaite/Headquarters (10/5-6), Bike & Hike/East Rim Trailhead & Ira Trailhead (10/6-7), Canal Exploration Center (10/7-8), Station Road Bridge Trailhead (10/13-15), Lock 39 Trailhead (10/15-16). Scheduled dates and times are subject to change due to weather conditions.

alerts.title: Eastern Section of Beech Mountain Loop Trail Closed for Repairs
alerts.description: Starting Sept 21, the eastern section of the Beech Mountain Loop Trail will be closed for repairs from a junction just beyond the parking lot to just below the summit at the fire tower. Three alternate routes to the summit are available: the outer loop of the Beech Mountain Loop Trail, Beech South Ridge Trail and Beech West Ridge Trail.

alerts.title: Schoodic Mountain Road Closed for Repairs
alerts.description: Starting Aug 31, the Schoodic Mountain Road will be closed for repairs from Schoodic Loop Road to the summit of Schoodic Head. Workers will be operating heavy equipment for resurfacing, regrading and ditching.

alerts.title: Trail Closures Due to Recent Rains
alerts.description: Wall Street is closed until further notice. Other park trails are open but muddy, and hikers are urged to use caution.

alerts.title: Watchman Trail closed
alerts.description: The Watchman Trail is closed pending repairs.

alerts.title: Vehicle Break-in and Theft Warning
alerts.description: Do not leave valuables in your car. As a last resort, lock items in your trunk before arriving. Thieves target parking lots and break-ins can occur.

alerts.title: Partial Trail Closures on Bailly / Chellberg Trail
alerts.description: Portions of Bailly / Chellberg Trail (with stairs) will be closed through October (10/30/26), to allow completion of boardwalk replacement project.

alerts.title: Towpath Trail between Boston and Peninsula
alerts.description: Closed from Boston Trailhead to Lock 29, August 24–November 20, 2026 and March 29–April 21, 2027.

alerts.title: Current East Rim Trail Status: Open
alerts.description: As of Wednesday, September 16, 2026, the East Rim Trail System remains open. For more information, visit the website linked below. In good conditions the mountain bike trails are open 6 am-11 pm for bikers and as posted for other trail users. In wet or hazardous conditions, the trail will close to all users to prevent damage. Be flexible; conditions may change throughout the day.

alerts.title: Large vehicle restrictions on Zion-Mt. Carmel Highway
alerts.description: Vehicles that exceed length, width, height, or weight limits cannot travel between Canyon Junction and the park's East Entrance. See the current limits on the page linked below.

alerts.title: Toxic cyanobacteria in rivers, streams, and pools
alerts.description: Do not submerge your head in or drink instream water in Zion National Park.

alerts.title: Angels Landing Pilot Permit Program
alerts.description: All hikers need a permit to hike Angels Landing. Learn why you need a permit and how to get one using the link below.

alerts.title: Southern Section of Ocean Path Closed for Repairs
alerts.description: Starting Aug 31, a section of Ocean Path will be closed for repairs from a trailhead across from the Otter Point parking lot to the trail's southern terminus.

alerts.title: Please park legally and responsibly
alerts.description: Zion has limited parking. Once parking spaces in Zion are full, visitors should park in Springdale. Please park only in designated spaces. Vehicles parked outside of designated spaces are subject to citation and towing.

alerts.title: West Thumb Geyser Basin Boardwalk - Partial Closure
alerts.description: A section of the West Thumb Geyser Basin boardwalk will be closed to Fishing Cone and Lakeshore Geyser through mid-October while crews replace damaged support structures along the shoreline. The remaining sections of boardwalk will remain open to visitors. Dates are subject to change without notice.

alerts.title: Partial Trail Closure - Dunewood Trace
alerts.description: Partially open. Persistent flooding west of the campground currently limits access to the entire trail. Hikers may not always be able to traverse the full length.

alerts.title: Closure - Hobart Woodland Trail
alerts.description: Closed. The Woodland Trail is closed indefinitely, and no reopening date is available. However, the paved Oak Savannah Trail remains open.

alerts.title: Partial Closure - Upland Trail
alerts.description: The middle boardwalk was lost due to a tree strike, making the full loop inaccessible. At this time, there is no timeline for replacement.

alerts.title: Closure - Heron Rookery Trail
alerts.description: Closed. The trail is undergoing tree removal and rerouting due to riverbank collapse. It is expected to reopen in the fall, after mosquito activity decreases.

alerts.title: Other Park Conditions and Updates
alerts.description: For more information on storm related repairs and other park conditions like beach and hiking safety visit our park status page.

alerts.title: Current Fire Restrictions
alerts.description: Fires are only allowed in established fire pits.

alerts.title: Stay Away From Bull Elk
alerts.description: Bull elk are fast and unpredictable this time of year and can seriously injure people. If an elk charges, run. In addition to staying at least 25 yards (23 m) away from elk and bison, always stay at least 100 yards (91 m) away from bears and wolves.

alerts.title: Water Safety Alert
alerts.description: After recent storms, E. coli levels are likely to reach above safe swimming standards. Entering the water after heavy rainfall is never recommended. Know before you go and always check our Beach Safety page before heading to park beaches.

alerts.title: Burn Ban in Park
alerts.description: Due to high fire danger, Hot Springs National Park has enacted a BURN BAN, August 15, 2026. Only gas and charcoal grills are currently allowed for use in the campground and picnic areas.

alerts.title: Partial Closures to Little Calumet River Trail and Glenwood Dunes Trail
alerts.description: Marquette Greenway construction will require closing sections of the Glenwood Dunes Trail (April–December 2026) and Little Calumet River / Mnoké Prairie Trail (May–December 2026). Closure dates may shift as work progresses. Please follow all posted closures and check the park website or NPS App for updates.

alerts.title: Biscuit Basin Closed Due to Hydrothermal Explosion
alerts.description: The parking lot, boardwalk, and Firehole River at Biscuit Basin, located north of Old Faithful, is closed to all travel until further notice due to the possibility of another event at the site of a hydrothermal explosion that occurred July 23, 2024.

alerts.title: Partial Trail Closure at Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk
alerts.description: Closed portion of Portage Lakefront and Riverwalk Trail along Burns Waterway due to unsafe conditions from erosional damage. This trail portion will remain closed while funding is sought for repair work. Pier access remains open on either side of closure.

alerts.title: Oasis of Mara Trail Partial Closure
alerts.description: Due to a heavy flooding event, the Oasis of Mara Trail is closed past the Oasis.

alerts.title: Traffic Delays - Gardner River High Bridge
alerts.description: Expect a single lane of traffic with up to 15-minute delays, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, from April 1 through late October 2026. Oversized/overweight vehicles (8'6"+ wide, 75'+ long, 80,000 lbs+ gross vehicle weight) will not be able to cross the bridge during this time.

alerts.title: Vehicle Entrance Reservation Not Needed
alerts.description: Although an entrance pass is required to enter Yellowstone National Park, vehicle reservations are not needed. You are encouraged to purchase an entrance pass before arriving, but you may also purchase passes at any entrance station upon arrival.

alerts.title: Expect Crowding
alerts.description: Parking lots and popular destinations are crowded especially on weekends and days with warm weather between 10 am and 3 pm.

alerts.title: Inaccurate Third-Party Apps
alerts.description: Some third-party hiking apps are providing inaccurate trail and safety information to users. Please use the official NPS app for accurate information.

alerts.title: Glacier Point Road is temporarily closed due to the Dome Fire
alerts.description: The Dome Fire is burning in the wilderness northeast of Wawona. Glacier Point Road is temporarily closed because of reduced visibility along the road due to smoke and to safely allow firefighting operations. Additionally, there are some trail closures south of Glacier Point Road.. Smoky conditions are possible at times.

alerts.title: Construction on HWY 26/89/191
alerts.description: Construction taking place on US HWY 26/89/191 south of Moran Junction. Expect 20-minute delays in both directions.

alerts.title: Crews Responding to Mount Tom Creek Fire
alerts.description: Fire managers are responding to a lightning fire in a remote area of Olympic National Park. The Mount Tom Creek Fire has burned 69 acres 5 miles west-northwest of Mount Olympus. Firefighters are using indirect confinement tactics as part of a full-suppression strategy. There are no evacuation orders or closures.

alerts.title: Construction in the South End of the Park
alerts.description: Moose-Wilson Road between Moose and LSR Preserve closed. Expect occasional short delays between Granite Entrance and LSR Preserve. Possible intermittent delays on Teton Park Road at Cottonwood Creek Picnic Area. Cottonwood Creek picnic area closed. Taggart Trail detour in place. Mormon Row area open with some construction activity.

alerts.title: Overnight Lodging Suspended and Parkwide Stage 4 Water Restrictions
alerts.description: Grand Canyon National Park has implemented Stage 4 water restrictions on the South Rim due to extensive flash flood damage to the Transcanyon Waterline. Overnight accommodations are suspended, and only dry camping is allowed. The park remains open for day use, with food and beverage services, the Grand Canyon Clinic, and Post Office remaining open. Visitors are asked to bring water with them when visiting the park.

alerts.title: Highway 101 Closed at Hoh River Bridge
alerts.description: The Highway 101 closure cuts off the only direct route between some of the most popular areas of the park. There are no detours available. Taking alternate routes around the east side of the Olympic Peninsula will add at least four hours to travel times.

alerts.title: INNER CANYON TRAIL CLOSURES
alerts.description: Current trail closures: The entire North Kaibab Trail (including Cottonwood Campground), Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, Silver Bridge, the South Kaibab Trail below Tip-Off, the River Trail east of the River Resthouse to the South Kaibab Trail junction, and the Black Bridge. Please do not attempt to access the closed areas.

alerts.title: INNER CANYON WATER SHUTOFFS
alerts.description: Beginning Sep. 6, no potable water will be available in the inner canyon, including along the Bright Angel Trail (1.5 Mile Resthouse, 3-Mile Resthouse, Havasupai Gardens day use and campground). All backpackers and hikers should carry water filtration and treatment OR carry all water with them.

alerts.title: South Shore Quinault Road Washed Out Beyond Park Boundary
alerts.description: South Shore Road – which is maintained by Jefferson County – is closed due to a major wash-out. For more information, visit the Jefferson County website.

alerts.title: Bat Tests Positive for Rabies, Visitors Urged to Report Potential Contact
alerts.description: A rabid bat was found at Olympic National Park near Staircase Bridge on August 9th. At approximately 2 p.m., the bat swooped down onto an unidentified woman and was temporarily caught in her hair. This individual is at risk for rabies and should seek healthcare immediately, as well as contact the Mason County Health Department at 360-427-9670 ext. 405. More at the link.

alerts.title: Mora Road Closed for Essential Repairs
alerts.description: Mora Road is closed to all traffic, including bicycles and pedestrians, at the campground. Rialto Beach is not accessible via Mora Road during this construction period. Mora Campground is open. This construction work will repair damage from a severe winter flood event, fortify the road against river migration, and protect long-term access to Rialto Beach.

alerts.title: Staircase Developed Area is Open, Use Caution in Burned Areas
alerts.description: The Staircase developed area is open. The surrounding wilderness areas will remain closed as repair and recovery efforts continue. Use extreme caution when entering burned areas. Burned landscapes may contain falling trees and branches, loose boulders, unstable ground, stump holes, landslides, and debris flows. Changing conditions such as wind, rain, or storms can rapidly trigger hazards. Learn more on our Fire Conditions and Updates page.

alerts.title: Critical Backcountry Updates/Closures
alerts.description: Visit this link for the inner canyon weather forecast, current trail closures, today's heat risk, and drinking water availability.

alerts.title: Going-to-the-Sun Road is Open for 2026 Season
alerts.description: The Going-to-the-Sun Road is fully open for the 2026 summer season. The road may now be accessed by motorized vehicles over Logan Pass from both the West Glacier and St. Mary Entrances.

alerts.title: Death Canyon Trailhead Construction Closure
alerts.description: Death Canyon Road and Trailhead are closed to all use. Start hikes at alternative trailheads such as Granite Canyon, LSR Preserve, and Taggart Lake.

alerts.title: Trip-planning tips for 2026
alerts.description: Planning to visit Arches this year? To ensure the best experience, please anticipate potentially long wait times at the entrance station. If trailhead parking is full, plan to return a little later. Please avoid parking on vegetation and roadways to help preserve this beautiful place for everyone to enjoy.

alerts.title: Trip-planning tips for 2026
alerts.description: Planning to visit Canyonlands this year? To ensure the best experience, please anticipate potentially long wait times at the entrance station. If overlook or trailhead parking is full, plan to return a little later. Please avoid parking on vegetation and roadways to help preserve this beautiful place for everyone to enjoy.

alerts.title: List of trail closures post-Hurricane Helene
alerts.description: Many closures remain on the Trail following Hurricane Helene's devastation. This will remain true for the foreseeable future. Visit the Appalachian Trail Conservancy (ATC) website for an up-to-date list of closures. OBSERVE ALL CLOSURES. Stay safe!

alerts.title: Black Bears Frequenting the McAfee Knob Area in Virginia
alerts.description: Human-habituated bears have been frequently spotted in the McAfee Knob Area. Allowing bears access to human food or garbage causes it to lose its fear of humans. Follow all food storage regulations, use provided food lockers and never feed a bear.

alerts.title: Forest Service Road 125 (Skyline Drive) Closure through December -James River and Warm Springs RD
alerts.summary: Forest Service Road 125 D (Skyline Drive) will be closed for repairs to address storm damage and to make improvements to drainage. The closure will likely last until the end of December 2026.

alerts.title: Bolar Mountain Recreation Area - Twin Ridge Road Closure
alerts.summary: Twin Ridge Road, just beyond the turn off for the beach facility at Bolar Mountain Recreation Area (Bath County, VA) will be temporarily closed to motor vehicles until approximately 9/21/2026. The closure affects the last mile of Twin Ridge Rd. Future closures of this road are expected due to…

alerts.summary: Geological Hazard Closures:FSR 700 (Little Stoney): State Route 822 to FSR 701.FSR 641 (Wallen Ridge): Baxley Lane to State Route 611.FSR 805 (Hanging Rock): Off State Route 72 @ Hanging Rock Entrance.FSR 239 (Maple Gap / Stock Creek): State Route 725 to FS gate.General Road Repair Closures:FSR 239…

alerts.title: James River Warm Springs Ranger District Office Offering Permits Only Wednesdays to Fridays
alerts.summary: Currently, the James River Warm Springs Ranger District Office in Hot Springs, VA, will issue permits only Wednesday through Friday each week, excluding holidays. We appreciate your understanding and apologize for any inconvenience.

alerts.title: Grindstone Campground and Parking Closed for 2026
alerts.summary: Grindstone Campground and its parking area will be closed for the remainder of the 2026 season due to the replacement of aging infrastructure and damage caused by Hurricane Helene. For Safety reasons please limit entry into the construction area. Sorry for any inconvenience this may cause and thank…

alerts.title: Eastern Divide District Road Closures
alerts.summary: The George Washington and Jefferson National Forest has announced that Schoolhouse Hollow Road and Pocahontas near Blacksburg, VA, will be closed for road maintenance work beginning June 1st.

alerts.title: Powell Mountain roads temporarily closed
alerts.summary: The George Washington and Jefferson National Forest has announced that Sentry Road on Powell Mountain in the Clinch Ranger District is temporarily closed for road maintenance.Once work is complete on Sentry Road, crews will move to Maple Gap Road (239) then Jasper Cliff Road (294). Road closures…

alerts.title: Fire Restrictions in place for Appalachian Trail
alerts.summary: In response to elevated fire danger, the George Washington and Jefferson National Forest has instituted fire restrictions within a quarter mile of the Appalachian National Scenic Trail as it passes through the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area. Building, maintaining, attending or using a fire,…

alerts.title: Virginia Creeper National Recreation Trail Closure Update
alerts.summary: The closed area around the Virginia Creeper National Recreation Trail now includes Trestle 16 and Trestle 17 near the Town of Damascus as construction activity is underway in this area. Currently, the section of the Virginia Creeper Trail from Trestle 16 in the Town of Damascus to the North…

alerts.title: Virginia Creeper Trail Reconstruction Closures
alerts.summary: The Virginia Creeper National Recreation Trail between Damascus and Whitetop Mountain remains closed due to significant safety concerns and ongoing recovery work following Hurricane Helene. There will be ongoing construction work in the area, beginning immediately. There are a number of…

alerts.title: Virginia Creeper Trail Contract Award
alerts.summary: The George Washington and Jefferson National Forest awarded Kiewit Corporation a contract valued at $240,580,430 to lead the full rebuild of the Virginia Creeper Trail following last year’s hurricane damage. The Virgina Creeper Trail is an iconic landmark that is an important economic and…

alerts.title: Mount Rogers National Recreation Area: Forest Service Road 84 Closed Beginning 9/1/25
alerts.summary: Mount Rogers National Recreation Area, Forest Service Road 84 is schedule to close 9/1/25 due to road maintenance. All dispersed camping along this road will be closed. Hurricane campground will remain open, users will still be able to access Hurricane Campground access via SR 650.

alerts.title: Construction near Appalachian Trail on Peter's Mountain
alerts.summary: Hikers may hear sound or see lights in the vicinity of Symms Gap meadow on the crest of Peters Mountain (southbound mile 1544, northbound mile 649.1) Please stay on the Trail.

alerts.title: Sherando Lake visitor rules
alerts.summary: The following prohibitions apply within the Sherando Lake Recreation Area. Organized games on beach and swimming area.Swimming outside the hours of 6:00 am to 8:00 pm.Swimming beyond outer rope and buoy markers.Bringing boat into the swimming area.Bringing glass bottles and other materials to the…

alerts.title: Saint Mary's Wilderness Prohibitions
alerts.summary: Several prohibitions are in place at the Saint Mary's Wilderness on the Glenwood-Pedlar Ranger District.It is prohibited to enter the wilderness area in a group larger than 10 people. Do not store personal property or dispose of trash anywhere in the wilderness area. Camping is not allowed within…

alerts.title: Special regulations apply when visiting wilderness areas
alerts.summary: When visiting wilderness areas in the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests, is it prohibited to:Enter the wilderness area in a group larger than ten people.Store personal property in the wilderness area.Disposing of trash anywhere in the wilderness area. alerts.title: Target shooting allowed only at designated shooting ranges
alerts.summary: For public safety, target shooting is allowed only in designated shooting ranges. It is prohibited to discharge a firearm within the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests unless you are target shooting in a designated shooting range or hunting following state hunting laws.

alerts.title: Shooting Ranges rules and prohibitions
alerts.summary: Target shooting on the George Washinton and Jefferson National Forests is allowed only at established shooting ranges. Several rules apply to all shooting ranges. See the below forest order for details.

alerts.title: Prohibitions in designated recreation sites
alerts.summary: Several prohibitions related to swimming, camping, and parking apply in Recreation Areas, Day Use sites, and swim beaches on the George Washington and Jefferson National Forest lands. See the below forest order for full details.

alerts.title: The abandoned Powells Fort Organization Camp is closed to all entry
alerts.summary: It is prohibited to enter within 100 feet of the abandoned buildings of the Powells Fort Organization Camp on the Lee Ranger District.

alerts.title: Vehicle requirements for use of Peters Mill Run/Taskers Gap Trail System
alerts.summary: Only four-wheel drive vehicles, all-terrain vehicles, motorcycles, or similar high clearance vehicles are allowed at the Peters Mill Run/Taskers Gap Trail System. Vehicle operators must have a valid state operator’s license as required by state law and vehicles my be registered with the State…

alerts.title: Motor vehicle operators must follow State Laws
alerts.summary: Motor vehicle operators must follow all State Laws.

alerts.title: Hunting prohibited around Lake Moomaw
alerts.summary: Hunting is prohibited in and around Lake Moomaw recreation areas.

alerts.title: Prohibitions on the James River Footbridge on the Appalachian National Scenic Trail
alerts.summary: It is prohibited to have alcohol, camp, or build a fire on or around the James River footbridge of the Appalachian National Scenic Trail or in the nearby parking lot on the Amherst County side of the footbridge. It is also prohibited to climb on any part of the bridge abutments or piers or jump…

alerts.title: General Prohibitions
alerts.summary: There are several general prohibitions that apply throughout the George Washington and Jefferson National Forest. See the attached forest order for details.

alerts.title: Food Storage and Disposal Requirements - Bear Safety
alerts.summary: In many campgrounds and recreation areas on the forest, visitors are required to store and dispose of food in bear-proof receptacles.

alerts.title: Controlled Substances Prohibited
alerts.summary: It is prohibited to possess controlled substances on National Forest lands in the George Washington and Jefferson National Forests.

alerts.title: Prohibitions at Cascades Recreation Area
alerts.summary: Climbing the rocks around or under the waterfall is prohibited. Camping anywhere in the recreation area, parking lot, or trail is prohibited. The trail is designated for hiking only. Horses, bikes, and motorized vehicles are prohibited on the trail. Alcohol is prohibited anywhere in the…

alerts.title: Alcohol prohibition at the Appalachian Trail Partnership Shelter
alerts.summary: Alcohol is prohibited at the Appalachian Trail Partnership Shelter on the Mount Rogers National Recreation Area.
